title: Constraint backend bridge: tokenizer escape handling and toolcall streaming framing
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds a bridge layer between constrained-decoding backends and the tokenizer to prevent streaming boundary corruption; fixes toolcall framing when constraints span token boundaries; backwards-compatible fallback to previous constraint APIs.
description: Motivation: In production we observed intermittent corruption when constrained decoders (CFG/regex backends) interacted with streaming frames: constraints could be applied at a token-level boundary that did not align with UTF-8 or subword token boundaries, producing broken escape sequences and truncated toolcall payloads. This PR introduces a lightweight bridge layer that normalizes constraint spans against tokenizer atom boundaries and provides safe streaming framing for function/tool calls so that constraints never split an escape sequence or a toolcall JSON chunk. Summary of changes: 1) tokenizer_shim: a tokenizer-aware normalizer that converts constraint ranges from byte/character offsets into token-atom-safe ranges and attaches metadata flags for streaming. 2) constraint_bridge: orchestrator that mutates constraint backends (CFG and regex adapters) to operate on normalized ranges; also includes a compatibility fallback for older backends that still expect raw offsets. 3) streaming_toolcall: framing helper that ensures toolcall start/end markers are emitted on frame boundaries and that KV-cache-aware resumed streams re-hydrate partial atoms before constraint enforcement. 4) openai_compat adjustments: translator now understands escaped delimiters and merges adjacent constraint fragments into single enforced units for parity with existing OpenAI-compatible behavior. Testing and rollout: unit tests cover surrogate pair splits, multibyte UTF-8 edgecases, and subword-token overlap; integration tests run against the streaming harness and the OpenAI compatibility suite. Canary rollout planned: enable bridge for 10% of traffic for 48 hours with metrics gated on parse errors and token-level rejections. Backwards compatibility: default false feature-flag; when disabled behavior is identical to previous decoders. Implementation notes: performance overhead measured at +1.8% median latency for 1024-token chat workloads with constraints; internal benchmarks show a 75% reduction in parse-error incidents in constrained streaming scenarios. The patch is intentionally small, documented, and includes rollback plan.

fix(streaming): ensure toolcall framing emits boundary-safe markers
chore(openai-compat): translate escaped delimiters into merged constraint fragments
test: add integration cases for surrogate-pairs and partial-atom resumes
docs: document bridge behavior and canary rollout steps

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Observability wise, can we add a token-level metric to monitor the frequency of normalized spans? Maya: added 'decoder.normalized_spans.count' and a tag for backend-type in a follow-up commit.

Jordan Kim: Is the compatibility fallback going to be a runtime allocation hotspot? Maya: fallback path is only taken for legacy backends and uses pooled buffers; microbenchmarks added showing minimal allocations.

Eva Müller: Suggest adding a canary kill-switch in case streaming framing regresses. Maya: included a feature-flag and explicit canary kill-switch in deploy/feature_flags.yaml; tested dynamic toggle in staging.
Liam O'Connor: Approved after CI rerun. Jordan Kim: LGTM. Eva Müller: Approved.

notes_on_compatibility: Bridge is behind feature flag 'constraint_bridge.enabled'. When off, decoders receive original raw offsets. The translator provides a soft-fallback that rewrites legacy offsets into normalized token-atom ranges on the fly without changing public API fields. OpenAI compatibility: merged constraint fragments emulate earlier single-range semantics for tool/function calls to avoid user-visible behavioral diffs.
testing_summary: Unit tests: 48 new cases for UTF-8 multibyte, surrogate pairs, subword overlap. Integration: 10 deterministic scenarios plus 200 randomized seeds against streaming harness. Perf: +1.8% median token latency for constrained streams at 1024 context; end-to-end parse-error rate decreased from 0.9% to 0.22% in canary tests.
rollback_plan: Toggle 'constraint_bridge.enabled=false' via runtime flags which immediately reverts bridge usage; if issues persist, push short-lived hotfix that disables streaming framing changes and revert merge with emergency branch 'hotfix/rollback-82914'. Notify SRE and product via pager and Linear ENG-2142.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps grammar/regex backends' core unchanged and focuses on a thin normalization layer to avoid regressions. Docs updated with examples of constraint mapping for tokenizer-aware clients.
